newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan Central Bank sees higher July inflation.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan Central Bank sees higher July inflation.

text.p: Venezuela's recent salary increases will cause inflation to edge up in July, although the annual inflation target of 30 to 35 percent is still on track, Central Bank President Antonio Casas Gonzalez said.
"It's logical that it (inflation) rises a little this month, but it will be within our program," Casas told reporters.
Venezuela's inflation rate fell to 1.8 percent in June, the second lowest monthly price rise in the last five years, bringing the annual rate to 43.5 percent.
The government has set a goal of bringing inflation down to between 30 and 35 percent this year from 103.2 percent in 1996.
Casas said that the aim was to continue bringing down the monthly rate, but "with the adjustments that are being made in salaries it is very difficult to achieve this."

Government officials have called on private sector companies this week to raise salaries in accordance with an agreement reached with unions to reform the country's outdated severance payments system.
